{{Short description|German-Finnish biochemist}}
'''Michael Jeltsch''' (born July 28, 1969, Hemer/NW, [[Germany]]) is a German-Finnish researcher in the field of [[Biochemistry]]. He is a professor at the [[University of Helsinki]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Michael Jeltsch, University of Helsinki|website=research.med.helsinki.fi |date=13 February 2017 |url=http://research.med.helsinki.fi/cancerbio/jeltsch/index.html}}</ref> [[Finland]]. He has more than 70 publications.<ref>{{cite web|title=Publications|url=http://www.researcherid.com/rid/I-5340-2012|website=researcherid.com}}</ref> Jeltsch was the first to show that [[VEGF-C]] and [[VEGF-D]] are the principal growth factors for the [[lymphatic]] [[vasculature]]<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Jeltsch|first1=M|last2=Kaipainen|first2=A|last3=Joukov|first3=V|last4=Meng|first4=X|last5=Lakso|first5=M|last6=Rauvala|first6=H|last7=Swartz|first7=M|last8=Fukumura|first8=D|last9=Jain|first9=RK|last10=Alitalo|first10=K|title=Hyperplasia of lymphatic vessels in VEGF-C transgenic mice.|journal=Science|date=30 May 1997|volume=276|issue=5317|pages=1423–5|pmid=9162011|doi=10.1126/science.276.5317.1423}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Oh|first1=SJ|last2=Jeltsch|first2=MM|last3=Birkenhäger|first3=R|last4=McCarthy|first4=JE|last5=Weich|first5=HA|last6=Christ|first6=B|last7=Alitalo|first7=K|last8=Wilting|first8=J|title=VEGF and VEGF-C: specific induction of angiogenesis and lymphangiogenesis in the differentiated avian chorioallantoic membrane.|journal=Developmental Biology|date=1 August 1997|volume=188|issue=1|pages=96–109|pmid=9245515|doi=10.1006/dbio.1997.8639|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Achen|first1=MG|last2=Jeltsch|first2=M|last3=Kukk|first3=E|last4=Mäkinen|first4=T|last5=Vitali|first5=A|last6=Wilks|first6=AF|last7=Alitalo|first7=K|last8=Stacker|first8=SA|title=Vascular endothelial growth factor D (VEGF-D) is a ligand for the tyrosine kinases VEGF receptor 2 (Flk1) and VEGF receptor 3 (Flt4).|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America|date=20 January 1998|volume=95|issue=2|pages=548–53|pmid=9435229|doi=10.1073/pnas.95.2.548|pmc=18457|bibcode=1998PNAS...95..548A|doi-access=free}}</ref> and his research focuses on [[cancer drug]] targets and [[lymphangiogenesis]]. He has also contributed to other seminal publications in cell biology<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Mandriota|first1=SJ|last2=Jussila|first2=L|last3=Jeltsch|first3=M|last4=Compagni|first4=A|last5=Baetens|first5=D|last6=Prevo|first6=R|last7=Banerji|first7=S|last8=Huarte|first8=J|last9=Montesano|first9=R|last10=Jackson|first10=DG|last11=Orci|first11=L|last12=Alitalo|first12=K|last13=Christofori|first13=G|last14=Pepper|first14=MS|title=Vascular endothelial growth factor-C-mediated lymphangiogenesis promotes tumour metastasis.|journal=The EMBO Journal|date=15 February 2001|volume=20|issue=4|pages=672–82|pmid=11179212|doi=10.1093/emboj/20.4.672|pmc=145430}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Gerhardt|first1=H|last2=Golding|first2=M|last3=Fruttiger|first3=M|last4=Ruhrberg|first4=C|last5=Lundkvist|first5=A|last6=Abramsson|first6=A|last7=Jeltsch|first7=M|last8=Mitchell|first8=C|last9=Alitalo|first9=K|last10=Shima|first10=D|last11=Betsholtz|first11=C|title=VEGF guides angiogenic sprouting utilizing endothelial tip cell filopodia.|journal=The Journal of Cell Biology|date=23 June 2003|volume=161|issue=6|pages=1163–77|pmid=12810700|doi=10.1083/jcb.200302047|pmc=2172999}}</ref> with [[transgenesis]], [[protein engineering]], recombinant production and purification. In 2006, he developed a synthetic super-VEGF, using a library of VEGF [[:wikt:hybrid|hybrid]] molecules using a novel, non-random [[DNA]] family shuffling method.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Jeltsch|first1=M|last2=Karpanen|first2=T|last3=Strandin|first3=T|last4=Aho|first4=K|last5=Lankinen|first5=H|last6=Alitalo|first6=K|title=Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)/VEGF-C mosaic molecules reveal specificity determinants and feature novel receptor binding patterns.|journal=The Journal of Biological Chemistry|date=28 April 2006|volume=281|issue=17|pages=12187–95|pmid=16505489|doi=10.1074/jbc.m511593200|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Jeltsch completed his graduation, postgraduation, and postdoc at Molecular/Cancer Biology Lab, University of Helsinki, Helsinki, Finland. He worked as a researcher at Lymphatix Ltd. (now Ark Therapeutics) via Licentia Ltd., Helsinki, Finland (April 2006 – January 2007) and at Circadian Technologies via Vegenics Ltd. via Licentia Ltd., Helsinki, Finland (February 2007 – December 2011), where he was involved in the research on VEGF-C and VEGF-D as drugs and drug targets.<ref>{{cite web|title=Patent|website=patft1.uspto.gov |url=http://patft1.uspto.gov/netacgi/nph-Parser?patentnumber=6958147}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Patent|website=patft1.uspto.gov |url=http://patft1.uspto.gov/netacgi/nph-Parser?patentnumber=8455453}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Patent|website=patft1.uspto.gov |url=http://patft1.uspto.gov/netacgi/nph-Parser?patentnumber=7422741}}</ref> He worked as a Postdoctoral Fellow at the [https://wri.fi/ Wihuri Research Institute], Helsinki, Finland from January 2013 to August 2013. Since 2013, he is a Group leader and since 2020 Associate Professor for Pharmaceutical Protein Drug Research at the Faculty of Pharmacy at University of Helsinki, Helsinki, Finland. The Jeltsch lab is affiliated with the Drug Development Program and the Individualized Drug Therapy Research Program.<ref>{{cite web|title=Affiliation|website=lab.jeltsch.org |url=http://lab.jeltsch.org/}}</ref>

He was awarded Medix Prize by the [[Minerva Foundation Institute for Medical Research]] for best biomedical publication of the year in Finland in March 1997. In 2003, he received the Mandatum Prize for the best PhD thesis in the field of [[biotechnology]] in Finland. In 2015, he received the “Best Paper Award” in the category of Basic Science by ''Circulation'', the journal of the [[American Heart Association]] for his 2014 work,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Jeltsch|first1=M|last2=Jha|first2=SK|last3=Tvorogov|first3=D|last4=Anisimov|first4=A|last5=Läppänen|first5=V-M|last6=Holopainen|first6=T|last7=Kivelä|first7=R|last8=Ortega|first8=S|last9=Kärpänen|first9=T|last10=Alitalo|first10=K|title=CCBE1 Enhances Lymphangiogenesis via A Disintegrin and Metalloprotease With Thrombospondin Motifs-3–Mediated Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor-C Activation.|journal=Circulation|date=19 February 2014|volume=129|issue=19|pages=1962–71|pmid=24552833|doi=10.1161/circulationaha.113.002779|doi-access=free}}</ref> in which
he identified the molecular mechanism behind [[Hennekam syndrome]].<ref>{{cite web|title=The winner of the "Best Paper Award" of Circulation - Michael Jeltsch|website=med.helsinki.fi |date=10 June 2016 |url=http://www.med.helsinki.fi/english/news/2015/20150505_Jeltsch.html}}</ref>
